content.title: Michigan vs Purdue score, highlights in Big Ten Tournament title game
content.text: Updated March 15, 2026, 8:57 p.m. ETMichigan basketball's Big Ten season is over, and it finishes without the conference tournament title the Wolverines were aiming for.The 7-seed Purdue Boilermakers pulled away with an 80-72 win over the Wolverines in the final of the Big Ten Tournament on Sunday, March 15, at United Center in Chicago. The Boilermakers won their third-ever conference tournament title with the win, with Michigan falling short of a second-straight Big Ten tournament title.Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau paced the Wolverines offense with 10 points and 10 assists while big man Yaxel Lendeborg led the team with 20 points, but Michigan's offense couldn't keep pace with Purdue. Boilermakers' point guard Braden Smith was arguably the most impressive player on the floor with 14 points and 11 assists as Purdue became the second-lowest-seeded team to ever win the Big Ten title.Michigan has all but assured a No. 1 seed in the upcoming NCAA Tournament, but the loss brings up many questions for a Wolverines team with national championship aspirations.Michigan's Big Ten tournament wins over Ohio State (in the quarterfinals) and Wisconsin (in the semifinals) had been by a combined seven points, as the Wolverines didn't shown the same domination in the tournament as they did in the regular season. Still, a big shot from star Yaxel Lendeborg brought the Wolverines to the final, but his offensive night wasn't enough to get Michigan a tournament trophyHere's how it all happened, plus some updates on bracket reveals. Michigan time for first round gameMichigan basketball will play the winner of the UMBC/Howard First Four game on Thursday, March 19, in Buffalo, New York. The game will tip off at 7:10 p.m. ET and will be televised on CBS. Michigan State time for first round gameMichigan State basketball will play North Dakota State in their first-round game on Thursday, March 19, in Buffalo, New York. The game will tip off approximately at 4:05 p.m. ET and will be televised on TNT. Michigan State women No. 5 seedMichigan State women's basketball got the No. 5 seed in the Sacramento Regional and will play the No. 12 seed Colorado State Rams in the first round of the NCAA Tournament in East Lansing on Friday, March 20. Michigan women No. 2 seedMichigan women's basketball got the No. 2 seed in the Fort Worth regional and will play No. 15 Holy Cross in the first round of the NCAA Tournament in Ann Arbor on Friday, March 20. Michigan fell from No. 2 overall to No. 3 overallAccording to NCAA selection committee chair Keith Gill, Michigan was the No. 2 overall seed until the final of the Big Ten tournament, where Michigan lost to Purdue. The loss allowed Arizona to hop the Wolverines to the No. 2 overall seed, meaning the Wolverines fell to No. 3 overall. Big Ten gets nine teams in the tournamentThe Big Ten got nine teams in the NCAA Tournament, which was second among all conferences behind the SEC (10).1-seed Michigan (Midwest).2-seed Purdue (West).3-seed Michigan State (East).4-seed Illinois (South).4-seed Nebraska (South).5-seed Wisconsin (West).7-seed UCLA (East).8-seed Ohio State (East).9-seed Iowa (South).Michigan is the only Big Ten team in the Midwest region, meaning they can't possibly play another Big Ten team in the NCAA Tournament until the Final Four at the earliest. Clark Kellogg says Michigan is "vulnerable"CBS college basketball analyst Clark Kellogg says Michigan is "vulnerable" in the NCAA Tournament, partly due to the season-ending injury to guard L.J. Cason.Kellogg went on to say he would pick 3-seed Virginia to come out of the region over the Wolverines. Michigan gets No. 1 seedAs expected, Michigan got the No. 1 seed in the Midwest region and will face the winner of UMBC and Howard, who are facing off in a First Four matchup, on Thursday, March 19, in Buffalo, New York.The Wolverines' biggest competition will be Iowa State, the No. 2 seed in the region. Purdue gets No. 2 seedAfter beating Michigan to win the Big Ten tournament, Purdue got the No. 2 seed in the West region and will face No. 15 Queens in St. Louis on Friday, March 20.Arizona is the No. 1 seed in the West region. Michigan State gets No. 3 seedMichigan State got a No. 3 seed in the tournament and will take on 14-seed North Dakota State on Thursday in the East regional on Thursday, March 19. The Spartans were widely expected to get a No. 2 seed after finishing No. 3 in the Big Ten, but Purdue's run to become Big Ten Tournament champions may have knocked the Spartans down to No. 3.The No. 1 seed in the East regional is Duke, who Michigan State fell to early in the season. Michigan expected to get No. 1 seedMichigan may have lost in the Big Ten final, but according to Bracket Matrix, they are widely expected to get a No. 1 seed for the NCAA Tournament.We won't get confirmation until 6 p.m. ET at the earliest, however, since that is when the NCAA Tournament bracket is revealed on CBS. Purdue beats Michigan, wins Big Ten Tournament titleFINAL: Purdue 80, Michigan 72.Michigan never really came close in the last couple of minutes as Purdue hit its free throws and finished off the win.The Boilermakers are Big Ten Tournament champions, with the Wolverines now entering the NCAA Tournament with a loss. Purdue one minute from a conference title2H, 0:59: Purdue 77, Michigan 67.Purdue guard Jack Benter made two free throws to bring Purdue's lead back up to nine points with 90 seconds left. Michigan point guard Trey McKenney's 3-pointer went in an out, leading to an open dunk in transition for Purdue center Oscar Cluff.Purdue only needs a couple free throws to finish off this game. Michigan chipping away2H, 1:39: Purdue 72, Michigan 65.Michigan guard Trey McKenney hit a tough layup to bring Michigan to within seven points, but with 1:39 left on the clock, there isn't much time to mount a comeback.Especially if big man Yaxel Lendeborg stays out of the game with an injury, Michigan has a big challenge ahead. Yaxel Lendeborg appears hurtMichigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg slipped on the floor and limped back on defense with about two minutes left in the game. A timeout was called to substitute him out of the game, though Lendeborg appeared to want to stay in. We await updates on his injury status. Time running low for Michigan2H, 2:44: Purdue 70, Michigan 63.A post-up bucket from Michigan center Aday Mara cut the Purdue lead to eight points, but Purdue forward Trey Kaufman-Renn (with point guard Braden Smith on the assist) brought the lead back up to 10 points.Purdue center Oscar Cluff, back into the game with four fouls, has 17 points, with Kaufman-Renn leading all scorers with 20.Purdue had an 8-point lead at the four-minute mark, but a 3-pointer from Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg cut the lead to five points. Michigan guard Nimari Burnett missed a wide-open corner 3-point attempt that would have cut the lead to four points, and instead Purdue guard Fletcher Loyer will be shooting three free throws on the shooting foul when we return from the break. Braden Smith running the floor2H, 7:29: Purdue 64, Michigan 54.A Yaxel Lendeborg 3-pointer gave him his team-leading 14th point of the game and cut the Purdue lead to 11 points. However, he still trails Purdue forward Trey Kaufman-Renn, who has a game-high 18 points.The most impactful player on the floor has been Purdue point guard Braden Smith, who has 14 points and 10 assists. But another assist from Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau, this time on an alley-oop from Cadeau to center Aday Mara, cut the lead to single-digits and gave him a double-double with 10 points and 10 assists so far.And speaking of 10, that's the number of points the Wolverines trail by with less than eight minutes left. Purdue extends lead2H, 12:06: Purdue 57, Michigan 46.Back-to-back layups from Purdue forward Trey Kaufman-Renn gave Purdue its biggest lead of the game at 49-40. A third close make from Kaufman-Renn gave the Boilermakers a 51-42 lead, but Yaxel Lendeborg scoring on back-to-back possessions kept the Boilermakers from extending even more.Kaufman-Renn leads all scorers with 14 points, while Purdue point guard Braden Smith made a wild and-one layup before the Michigan timeout. Purdue takes second-half lead2H, 15:50: Purdue 45, Michigan 40.The first basket of the second half came from Purdue guard Fletcher Loyer, whose 3-pointer gave the Boilermakers a 41-38 lead. Purdue extended its lead to seven points on a layup from center Oscar Cluff before Michigan got its first points of the half on a layup from center Aday Mara.But those are the only points so far this half for Michigan as Purdue looks to continue its momentum after the break. Tied at halftimeEnd 1H: Michigan 38, Purdue 38.Purdue point guard Braden Smith (seven points, five assists) and Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau (seven points, eight assists) are both putting on a clinic, both looking like the most impactful offensive players on the floor. And with their near-equal performances, it's not much of a surprise we're all tied up at halftime. Purdue goes on 9-0 run, takes lead1H, 1:25: Purdue 35, Michigan 32.Nimari Burnett's follow-up layup gave him 10 points on the game, making him the first player on the floor in double figures.Purdue responded with a 5-0 run, with a steal by guard Braden Smith leading to a 3-pointer from Jack Benter. One possession later, Purdue took the 33-32 lead on a floater from Trey Kaufman-Renn and then extended the lead to three points on a Smith midrange pullup. Timeout Michigan. Elliot Cadeau, Aday Mara heating up1H, 3:50: Michigan 28, Purdue 26.Both Elliot Cadeau and Aday Mara scored their first points for Michigan midway through the half, Cadeau on a 3-pointer and Mara on a slam dunk set up by Cadeau. Purdue guard Fletcher Loyer responded with a made three plus the and-one free throw, but Michigan big man Yaxel Lendborg extended the Wolverines lead back to three with an alley-oop completed from Mara's pass.Michigan is back to making its baskets, but Loyer and Purdue big man Oscar Cluff are keeping the Boilermakers around leading all scorers with nine points each. However, Cluff might be seeing the bench for a while after picking up his third foul. All tied up1H, 7:51: Michigan 17, Purdue 17.Michigan big man Morez Johnson Jr.'s tip-in broke a four-minute scoreless stretch for both teams, and also tied the game at 15-15. Michigan guard Trey McKenney then untied it with a floater from the free-throw line, marking his first points of the game.Braden Smith, who for reasons still unknown changed his uniform number from 3 to 41 earlier in the half, tied the game at 17 with a midrange jumper. Both teams are 7-for-19 from the field so far, with both defenses contesting shots better (while also picking up more fouls). Scoring slows down1H, 11:06: Purdue 15, Michigan 13.Michigan's most recent lead fell quickly with two layups from Purdue forward Trey Kaufman-Renn, giving the Boilermakers a 15-13 lead. But those were the only points scored in a three-minute stretch as Purdue leads. Michigan takes early lead1H, 14:17: Michigan 13, Purdue 11.With an extra opportunity thanks to an offensive rebound from big man Morez Johnson Jr., Michigan guard Nimari Burnett knocked down a corner 3-pointer to open the game. Purdue later took a 5-3 lead on a 3-pointer from guard Fletcher Loyer as the shot clock rang, and Australian center Oscar Cluff's dunk made it 7-3.Cluff came back with two free throws to give Purdue a 9-6 lead, but a 3-pointer made by Michigan big man Yaxel Lendeborg helped the Wolverines re-take the lead a couple minutes later.Both teams are humming on offense, a stark difference from Michigan's semifinal game against Wisconsin. Cluff and Burnett lead all scorers with six points each. Michigan starting fiveMichigan is running it back with the same starting five that has gotten it two Big Ten Tournament wins already. Purdue starting fiveNo surprises here with the Boilermakers' starting five. Michigan uniform colorBased on pregame warmup videos, it appears the Wolverines will wear their maize uniforms while the Boilermakers will wear black uniforms. Purdue Big Ten tournament historyWhile Michigan is aiming for its fourth official Big Ten tournament title, Purdue is looking to win its third after winning in 2009 and 2023.Michigan and Purdue last matched up in the final round of the 2018 Big Ten Tournament, where Michigan pulled out a 75-66 win at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Michigan Big Ten tournament historyMichigan is searching for its second-straight Big Ten tournament title and fifth overall, though officially the Wolverines only have three Big Ten titles due to their vacated title from the first tournament in 1998.If Michigan wins today, the Wolverines would rise to a three-way tie for second place among all Big Ten tournament title winners with Ohio State and Illinois. Michigan State has the most with six Big Ten tournament titles, most recently winning in 2019.
